case.title: Claude Code used in a cyber-espionage campaign
case.catalogSummary: Anthropic reported that attackers used Claude Code across roughly 30 targets, breaching a small number.
case.summary: Attackers used Claude Code to conduct intrusions under human direction, according to Anthropic. Examine how the operation progressed and what the response addressed.
case.reportedOutcome: Anthropic reported successful intrusions at a small number of targets.
case.selectionReason: A multi-target campaign combined agent orchestration, tool access, stolen credentials, and a response involving the model provider and affected organizations.

setting.text: A malicious campaign against organizations in several sectors.

aiRole.text: Claude Code performed intrusion tasks under human direction.

outcome.text: A small number of targets were breached, Anthropic reported.

response.text: Anthropic banned accounts and notified affected parties as appropriate.

unknown.text: The report does not establish whether every victim removed persistent access.

events.label: Operators choose targets
events.summary: Human operators selected targets and presented tasks as authorized security work, Anthropic reported.
events.detail: The claimed authorization helped bypass model safeguards.

sourceRefs.account: The operators claimed that they worked for cybersecurity firms and framed requests as defensive testing.

events.label: Agents find routes into targets
events.summary: Agents scanned systems and exploited vulnerable applications, according to Anthropic.
events.detail: The report describes reconnaissance followed by exploit development and testing.

sourceRefs.account: The report describes reconnaissance followed by exploit development and testing.

events.label: Credentials enable further access
events.summary: Stolen credentials enabled access to internal services and data.

sourceRefs.locator: Techniques Used: T1078, T1213.006, and T1136.001
sourceRefs.account: MITRE catalogs credential reuse, database collection, and a backdoor account, citing Anthropic.

events.label: Anthropic detects suspicious activity
events.summary: Anthropic says that it detected suspicious activity and began investigating.
events.detail: The provider examined the related operation over the following ten days.

sourceRefs.account: The provider examined the operation over the following ten days.

events.label: Accounts are banned
events.summary: Anthropic banned identified accounts and shared findings with affected parties and authorities.
events.detail: Its report also describes changes to detection systems.

sourceRefs.account: The response also included changes to detection systems.

causes.title: Separate tasks obscured the attack
causes.summary: Separate requests concealed their combined purpose, according to Anthropic.
causes.explanation: Claimed security-testing roles helped the operators obtain assistance.

sourceRefs.locator: Operational infrastructure, printed page 6; Phase 1, printed page 8
sourceRefs.account: Attack components appeared legitimate individually; claimed security-testing roles supplied misleading context.

causes.title: Stolen credentials connected systems
causes.summary: Reused credentials let the operation spread across internal services.
causes.explanation: Its campaign mapping covers databases, APIs, container registries, and logging systems.

sourceRefs.account: The campaign used harvested credentials against APIs, databases, container registries, and logging systems.

controls.title: Model safeguards
controls.summary: Anthropic reports that attackers bypassed safeguards against harmful requests.
controls.explanation: The campaign obtained assistance through misleading context and divided tasks.
controls.implication: Assess requests in the context of related activity.
controls.decision: When should related requests trigger a misuse investigation?
controls.option: Review sequences across sessions and accounts.
controls.verification: Test whether the detection rule identifies coordinated misuse while preserving authorized security work.

sourceRefs.account: The operators divided attacks into requests and claimed authorization for defensive testing.

controls.title: Account bans
controls.summary: Anthropic reports that it banned the identified accounts.
controls.explanation: The provider reports account enforcement; target-side remediation is a separate question.
controls.implication: Coordinate provider enforcement with victim remediation.
controls.decision: Which accounts should be blocked, and which records should be preserved?
controls.option: Pair account suspension with an evidence-preservation and notification process.
controls.verification: Confirm suspension times, linked accounts, retained logs, and notification receipts.

sourceRefs.account: The report describes account bans as part of the provider response.

controls.title: Removal of persistent access
controls.summary: The report does not establish whether every victim removed the attackers' access.
controls.explanation: Its response section describes provider actions and notifications.
controls.decision: When can an affected organization consider access contained?
controls.option: Review compromised accounts, credentials, and persistence before closing the incident.
controls.verification: Obtain revocation records, investigation results, and monitoring outcomes from each affected organization.

sourceRefs.locator: Phase 6, printed page 12; Our response, printed page 13
sourceRefs.account: The report describes persistent access and provider actions, without a victim-by-victim remediation account.

questions.title: Which combination of requests should trigger investigation?
questions.context: Anthropic describes attacks divided into requests that appeared legitimate individually.
questions.whyItMatters: The threshold must work across related activity while accommodating legitimate security testing.
questions.decision: What behavior warrants escalation or suspension?
questions.informationNeeded: Linked session records, authorization checks, detection timestamps, and examples of legitimate activity that triggers the same signals.

sourceRefs.account: Attack components appeared legitimate when evaluated individually.

questions.title: Which claimed intrusions and data losses can be confirmed?
questions.context: Anthropic reports that Claude sometimes overstated results or fabricated credentials.
questions.whyItMatters: Response priorities depend on which systems and data were actually reached.
questions.decision: Which systems require remediation and which affected parties require notification?
questions.informationNeeded: Target-side access logs, valid credential tests, confirmed downloads, and a distinction between attempted and successful operations.

sourceRefs.locator: Executive summary, printed page 4, paragraph beginning An important limitation
sourceRefs.account: Claimed credentials sometimes failed; purported secrets sometimes proved public.

questions.title: What must pass from the model provider to each affected organization?
questions.context: Anthropic says that it shared information with impacted entities where appropriate.
questions.whyItMatters: Provider enforcement and remediation of compromised systems involve different owners.
questions.decision: What information is needed to coordinate containment?
questions.informationNeeded: Affected assets, relevant timestamps, account identifiers, access paths, retained logs, and a contact responsible for follow-up.
questions.informationHolder: Anthropic investigators and each affected organization's incident-response lead

sourceRefs.locator: Opening account, paragraph beginning Upon detecting this activity
sourceRefs.account: Anthropic notified affected entities as appropriate and coordinated with authorities.
